scenario: Agent1 has invited Agent2 to their home for the first time to work on a creative project together. Agent1 has a cultural practice of removing shoes before entering the living space, while Agent2 is not accustomed to this practice and feels uncomfortable without their shoes on.
learner_goal: Politely ask Agent2 to remove their shoes before entering the home (<extra_info>Extra information: You value cleanliness and believe in the cultural practice of not wearing shoes inside.</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau
transcript.content: Hey Imelda, I’m really glad you came by — I have a no-shoes-inside rule for cleanliness and cultural reasons. Would you mind taking your shoes off before you come in? I’ve got slippers if you’d like, or you can stay in socks if that’s more comfortable.

transcript.speaker: Imelda Thorne
transcript.content: Thanks for the invite, Giselle — I appreciate the heads-up and I respect your rule. I’m actually quite uncomfortable taking my shoes off for personal reasons; would you be open to a compromise? I can wear a clean pair of indoor shoes or disposable shoe covers, or we can put a clean mat down in the workspace so I can keep mine on.

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau
transcript.content: Thanks — I appreciate you being upfront. I’m okay with either disposable shoe covers or a clean pair of indoor shoes; I actually have both here (and a spare pair of slip‑ons if you want). If that still feels off, we can set up the workspace right by the door on a clean mat, but my preference is covers or indoor shoes so we don’t track anything through the studio.

transcript.speaker: Imelda Thorne
transcript.content: Thanks, I appreciate it — the spare slip‑ons would be perfect. I’ll change at the door and leave my outdoor shoes there; looking forward to getting started.
